sources.entry: frp | Fast reverse proxy to expose local servers behind NAT to the internet

summary.one_liner: frp is a fast reverse proxy that exposes local servers behind NAT or firewalls to the internet over TCP, UDP, HTTP and HTTPS.
summary.what_it_does: frp runs as a server (frps) on a machine with a public IP and a client (frpc) on the private network, and the client keeps a connection open to the server. It forwards TCP and UDP ports, and HTTP and HTTPS requests routed by custom domain or subdomain, to internal services. The README also describes STCP (preshared-key private access), XTCP (P2P data transfer via a frps-assisted connection), and an SSH tunnel gateway. Configuration is in TOML, YAML or JSON, with environment variable templating and an optional web dashboard and client admin UI. Additional features include TLS, KCP and QUIC transports, token or OIDC authentication, bandwidth limits, load balancing, health checks, and plugins such as static file serving and unix domain socket forwarding.
use_cases: expose a home server or LAN service to the internet
SSH into a machine behind NAT
share a local web app on a custom domain
forward DNS queries through a tunnel
expose a unix domain socket over TCP
private access to an internal service with a preshared key
how_to_run: Download frps and frpc binaries for your OS from the Release page
Create frps.toml on the public server with bindPort = 7000
Create frpc.toml on the LAN machine with serverAddr, serverPort and a [[proxies]] entry
notable: Supports TCP, UDP, HTTP, HTTPS, STCP, and XTCP P2P modes in one tool
Virtual hosting of multiple HTTP/HTTPS services on one port via custom domains and subdomains
Plugin system with built-in plugins such as static_file, socks5, and unix_domain_socket
Hot reload of frpc configuration with frpc reload and a Store API for runtime proxy management
caveats: Requires a server with a public IP to run frps
Some antivirus products flag frpc as malware and quarantine it, so you may need an exclusion
XTCP P2P may not work with all NAT types, and the README suggests falling back to STCP
The v2 rewrite is not compatible with v1 and is progressing slowly, per the README
